title: Observability: -ENOENT with no log when FIPS mode active and no provider of any kind handles algo
description: In crypto2dev_lookup_algo() (registry.c line 311-313), the 'FIPS mode: skipped non-FIPS provider' message only fires when skipped_non_fips is non-NULL — i.e., a non-FIPS provider was present but skipped. If neither a FIPS nor a non-FIPS provider has registered the requested algo (e.g. ctr(aes) when only wolfssl is loaded), the loop exits with ops=NULL, skipped_non_fips=NULL, and no log is emitted. ioctl_init's fallback at line 742 logs only 'not found — FIPS mode active; ensure a FIPS provider registers this algo'. A support engineer cannot tell from dmesg whether FIPS mode is active and ate the lookup, or whether the algo is simply unregistered — the distinction requires checking /sys/class/misc/crypto2dev/fips_enforcement separately.
close_reason: fd.c callers log 'FIPS mode active' vs 'no provider registered' based on crypto2dev_fips_provider_loaded() — support engineers can distinguish FIPS-filtered from completely-unregistered algo from dmesg alone. Registry-level log for skipped non-FIPS providers still fires when applicable. No additional registry log needed.
